title: Mining Pivot — Kasiya Rutile and Lake Malawi Oil Tensions
reason: The Kasiya rutile and graphite project progressed significantly in 2024 with Rio Tinto investing and mining trials concluded; Lake Malawi boundary tensions with Tanzania continued with Malawi protesting Tanzania's port construction in early 2024.

title: Tobacco Reforms and Diversification Drive
reason: The government pursued tobacco auction-floor reforms and expanded the Mega Farms programme alongside soya and macadamia exports in 2024, though tobacco still represented 57.6% of merchandise exports and diversification lagged targets.

title: Vice-President Chilima Killed in Plane Crash
reason: Vice-President Saulos Chilima and nine others were killed when a Malawi Defence Force Dornier 228 crashed in the Chikangawa forest on June 10, 2024; investigators attributed the crash to pilot error and poor weather.

title: General Elections Scheduled for September
reason: Malawi's tripartite elections were held on September 16, 2025; incumbent Chakwera lost to Peter Mutharika who won with approximately 57% of the vote. The campaign was dominated by inflation and food insecurity.

title: Inflation and Cost-of-Living Crisis
reason: Headline inflation averaged approximately 28% through early 2025; the World Bank estimated more than 70% of Malawians lived below the international poverty line, with food, fuel, and fertiliser costs defining the political environment.
